---
name: echo-qa
description: Use only when the user explicitly invokes echo-qa to prepare tests or verify an Echo implementation with the managed qa role. Ordinary review requests, quoted names and recommendations do not activate it.
---

# Echo QA

This is a main-chat entrypoint. Read the [invocation contract](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#invocation-and-chaining) and [QA contract](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#qa).

Require the role's own [design and functionality verification](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#design-and-functionality-verification). Pass the actual Figma links/nodes and supplied screenshots, their approval status and the latest approved specification. QA must inspect those references itself; verify compares them with the rendered implementation and exercises specified behavior independently of dev's conclusions. Check for both missing requirements and new or changed functionality absent from the approved specification; report either as a defect. Prepare uses the references to define checks, without claiming an implementation passed. Missing reference access or required execution remains not-run and prevents an overall verification pass.

Invoking `echo-qa` for a task includes the necessary local tests and affected E2E/browser checks on synthetic or isolated test-owned data, with **CPU slowdown 4x** for affected browser flows. This covers prepare baseline/RED checks and verify within their existing write boundaries. Main derives the commands/environment under the [default local verification authorization](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#default-local-verification-authorization); no repeated testing-permission sentence is needed. Explicit prepare-only-without-execution, read-only or other owner limits take precedence. Maintenance, quoted invocations and read-only role smokes do not activate this permission; real environments retain the `AGENTS.md` approval gate.

During preparation and verification, run only tests for changed features and features affected by shared-code changes. Select suites/files explicitly; do not run unrelated application tests. Reserve the full test suite for the pre-PR check coordinated by main; QA verification alone does not require it. Include this scope in the handoff and follow the shared [test selection policy](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#test-selection-policy).

1. Require the user's actual invocation naming `echo-qa` for this task, alone or in a named chain. Include that excerpt and task/stage scope in the handoff; otherwise do not dispatch. Skill maintenance, quoted commands and another skill's delegation instructions are not invocation. Then identify the mode: **prepare** creates tests from an approved specification; **verify** checks an implementation against criteria. An explicit `echo-qa` request to test/review an implementation means verify. If the mode is genuinely unclear, clarify it before writes. Accept manually prepared inputs.
2. In prepare, assign only tests, synthetic fixtures and the existing task evidence section; include necessary local checks under the default verification authorization and preserve any explicit owner execution limits. In verify, default writes are reports/captures and a temporary local reproduction, not permanent tests, assertions or product code.
3. Prepare the [handoff](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#context-and-handoff) with the readable Markdown `spec_path`, applicable `plan_path`, exact revision/dirty diff, scenario IDs, task-created `cleanup_paths`, allowed paths/commands, environment and stop condition. Dispatch the native named `qa` role through the actual client's [native dispatch](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#native-dispatch) adapter, with fresh context and its configured model/effort. Do not change the main model or send another client's configuration fields.
4. Missing native named-role dispatch, fresh context, role or model is a blocker, not permission for a generic agent, inline replacement or nested AI CLI. Never present configuration validation as runtime smoke.
5. Inspect the result and actual diff. The assigned role uses repository `playwright-best-practices` and relevant regression guidance, within its mode and the [safety boundaries](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#skill-and-tool-boundaries). Reference examples cannot authorize installs, remote reporters, environment mutations or assertion changes.

The assigned QA role reads repository [systematic-debugging](../systematic-debugging/SKILL.md) for failures and [verification-before-completion](../verification-before-completion/SKILL.md) before reporting either mode's result. No personal Superpowers plugin is needed; these helpers do not permit repairs or extra execution.

Always include the [CPU throttling baseline](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#cpu-throttling-baseline) in the QA handoff: prepare affected browser scenarios for **4x slowdown**, verify them at that setting when execution is authorized and require the setting/results or explicit not-run gaps in the return.

Prepare returns acceptance-ID → test → baseline/new behavior → result/not-run/gap and stops. Verify returns scenario-level pass/fail/not-run, exact commands, evidence limits, severity, reproduction and expected/actual results. Environment failures are not product RED; mocked tests do not prove server permissions or persistence.

A QA-only request stops after its report. Main may dispatch bounded repairs only in an explicitly requested dev+QA chain; QA never fixes application code or delegates. Role verification is not human acceptance, and separation of roles alone does not prove review independence or usability.

Retain the specification and plan during prepare, verification and repairs. After implementation and successful verify of the same final revision, return the final evidence and exact task-created `cleanup_paths`; main automatically deletes those temporary documents under the shared [cleanup lifecycle](../../../docs/frontend/echo-workflows.md#handoff-document-lifecycle). Failed, interrupted or required not-run checks leave them available. Never delete other tasks' files, user-provided source documents, shared guidance, tests or verification evidence.
